High and low water move by up to an hour a day, and by minutes between two beaches a few miles apart, so a tide time is the one thing I would not guess: a tide-table site for that beach, or the harbour or pier's own page, has today and tomorrow, and the local paper prints them too.

Two beaches a few miles apart turn minutes apart and the same one is an hour later tomorrow, so I can't hold today's times: the harbour's page or a tide table for that beach has them, with the height as well as the clock time - the height is the bit that matters if you are walking a causeway or launching a boat.
